segments.text: My ex-husband stared at me in the frozen aisle like he'd seen a ghost.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: I nearly cried there in the parking lot, but my sister flew in and proved it wasn't my fault.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: That Thursday, I came home too soon. Heard them upstairs in our room.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Thirty-one beside fifty-six in our bed. No scream, no tears, not one word said.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: I shut the door and sat in the dark 'til the midnight mirror tore me apart.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: At fifty-four, I barely knew the swollen face I was looking into.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Six months on my shot, the hunger was gone, but my belly stayed out, round and hard as a stone.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Walked every morning, kept the routine. Ate half of what I used to, ate clean.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Sulfur burps, bloat, four days without going. Worse every week, and I couldn't say why.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: I don't know her. Maybe he felt the same.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: I called my sister, Denise. Two years on the same shot as me.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: She'd been where I was, and she'd found the way.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: She flew in next day, no hug at the door. "We have work. You won't stay like this anymore."
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Two days in, she asked about my belly. "It's been like this since the second month."
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: She said, "You don't need to feel ashamed. You didn't even know what the shot had changed."
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: It slows your stomach down on purpose, that's how it works. So the food you ate just sits there. Not for hours. For days. It ferments, it bloats, it backs up, and the fiber and the MiraLAX just pile on more.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Six months pushing against a locked door. Your gut couldn't let go anymore.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: For the first time, I could finally see. It wasn't age, it wasn't me.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: More fiber won't push a slowed gut away. My body never betrayed me.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: She set two capsules in front of me. GLP-1 SOS, Daily Gut Relief.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Two hundred fifty milligrams of magnesium pulls water in gently and softens what's been sitting there for days.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Two hundred milligrams of ginger gets the stomach moving again, so nothing sits long enough to ferment.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Two with dinner. That's it.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Built for a slowed gut, not a normal one. It works with the shot, not against it.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Day three, the burps were gone.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Week two, mornings like clockwork.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Week four, the bloat was too.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: No other changes, I stayed on my shot. It just followed through.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Week six, my old black dress fit like new after a year hidden out of view.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Soon after, frozen aisle, she at his side. He stared like he couldn't believe his eyes.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: "You look incredible. What did you do?" I gave him silence, kept walking through.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: I felt his eyes 'til I left his view.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: He didn't leave because I grew old. He left when cowardice took hold.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: My body was never the one to blame. More fiber won't push a slowed gut away.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: The only thing that worked for me, GLP-1 SOS, finally.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Denise says it sells out all the time. I checked yesterday, and you're end of the line.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: If the button still shows below, get it before the last ones go.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: Sixty days, money back, no questions asked.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: And stop blaming yourself at all.
segments.speaker: Narrator

segments.text: This was never, ever your fault.
segments.speaker: Narrator
